core.title: Keep every plan identity unique
core.given: the scanned plan artifacts, each declaring an identity through the stack's identity keys
core.when: the plan is authored or validated — whether an artifact is being created, copied, renamed, or a duplicate already exists
core.then: ensure no two plan artifacts declare the same identity.
prefer: When a duplicate is found, rename one of the artifacts, or merge them.
Check the existing plan artifacts for the identity before declaring it in a new or copied artifact.
avoid: Copying an artifact as a template and leaving its identity unchanged.
Keeping two artifacts with the same identity and relying on whichever is read first to win.
Silencing the finding by moving a plan artifact into a vendored or generated tree.
unless: The artifacts live in trees that are never scanned (the profile's excluded vendored and generated trees).
core.why: A reference to a duplicated identity resolves to whichever file was read first, so references become ambiguous and order-dependent.
evidence: The plan-integrity check reports no duplicate identity across scanned plan artifacts.
Reviewer confirms each identity occurs in exactly one artifact declaration.
verification: A repository-wide plan-integrity check compares every declared identity key across all parsed scanned plan artifacts, including pre-existing duplicates that the current task did not introduce.
The check never scans the profile's excluded trees (vendored and generated trees); the exact list is the stack's one scan-exclusion list.
Per-rule enforcement: severity 3, disposition strict — every duplicate identity is a failure, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

fires: A plan artifact is added whose declared identity already exists in another plan artifact.
An existing plan artifact is copied as a template and its declared identity is left unchanged.
Two existing plan artifacts already declare the same identity when the plan is validated, even though the current task did not touch them.
doesNotFire: A duplicate identity appears only inside trees that are never scanned (the profile's excluded trees).
An artifact references another artifact's identity (a reference, not a declaration).
Every scanned plan artifact declares an identity that no other scanned artifact declares.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan artifact kinds that play the plan_artifact role and are scanned for declared identities, wherever they live.

profileRequirements.meaning: The identity keys by which plan artifacts declare their identity; uniqueness is enforced over the values they declare.

profileRequirements.meaning: The one stack-wide list of vendored and generated trees that are never scanned, where the rule does not apply.

neutralityNotes: The core names no stack, runtime, path or suffix. Three things are carried as data or realization detail instead of being neutralized in-place: (1) the concrete identity keys (train_id, interlocking_id, journey_id, urn, …) and plan artifact kinds (train, interlocking, journey, wagon, WMBT, acceptance, …) vary per stack — they come from profile keys roles.plan_artifact.kinds and the proposed urn.grammar#identity_keys (no existing vocabulary key lists the identity keys compared for uniqueness, so it is proposed in the urn group); (2) the never-scanned trees are the one stack-wide roots.excluded list (node_modules, dist, build, _generated in Bun), per the vocabulary's single-list rule; (3) the validator id planner_plan_integrity and the finding id duplicate-identity are realization details and stay bunOnly. Per-rule severity (3) and strict disposition stay in core verification, never in the profile. The rule scans plan artifacts wherever they live, so no plan-root path key is required.
